# ink — terminal markdown reader

## Overview

ink is a feature-rich terminal markdown reader built in Rust. It renders markdown with syntax highlighting, inline images, mermaid diagrams, and more inside an interactive TUI. It ships as a single binary with no runtime dependencies.

## Features

### Rendering
- Full GFM (GitHub Flavored Markdown) support via the comrak parser
- Headings (levels 1-6) with distinct visual styling and block prefixes
- Bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code
- Links with OSC 8 hyperlink support (Cmd+Click / Ctrl+Click in supported terminals)
- Syntax-highlighted code blocks using syntect (supports all major programming languages)
- Tables with auto-sized columns, word wrapping and column alignment (:--, :-:, --:)
- Blockquotes with nested support and depth-based coloring
- Ordered and unordered lists with nesting
- Task lists with checkbox rendering
- Footnotes
- Superscript <sup>x</sup> and subscript <sub>x</sub> as Unicode forms (^(x)/_(x) in ASCII mode) when the content is plain text that has them; otherwise (captions, links, markup) the content is shown as written; ^x^ and ||x|| are not syntax (carets and double bars in prose are shown as written); ~x~ and ~~x~~ are strikethrough as on GitHub; definition lists (Term / : definition)
- Horizontal rules
- Inline/block math ($...$, $$...$$, ```math) rendered as Unicode text: Greek letters, operators, \mathbb/\mathcal letters, super/subscripts, \frac as a/b, \sqrt, matrix/cases/aligned environments on several lines; unknown commands kept as written; ASCII mode shows the LaTeX source. A lone $ in prose stays a dollar sign. :emoji: shortcodes resolved to glyphs
- HTML blocks shown as text; common inline HTML (<br>, <sub>, <sup>, <kbd>) handled rather than dropped, <sub>/<sup> as Unicode sub/superscripts where possible
- YAML and TOML frontmatter: stripped by default; --frontmatter shows it as a key/value box. A leading JSON object is never stripped; with --frontmatter it is shown as the box only when markdown follows it

### Images
- Real pixel rendering via terminal graphics protocols (Kitty graphics, iTerm2 inline, Sixel), auto-detected at startup; --image-protocol auto|kitty|iterm2|sixel|halfblocks
- Falls back to Unicode half-block characters (▄) with 24-bit color on terminals without a graphics protocol (any true-color terminal)
- Images scroll with the document and clip cleanly at the viewport edges
- Loads images from local files (relative paths, contained to the document directory)
- Remote (http/https) images are OFF by default (shown as a placeholder); enable with --remote-images. Even then, private/loopback/link-local/cloud-metadata addresses are blocked, with timeouts and a 20 MB cap
- Decoded images are cached; falls back to emoji placeholder (🖼) if an image can't be loaded or decoded
- Respects --no-images flag

### Mermaid Diagrams
- Renders mermaid code blocks as text art; flowcharts, state, class and ER diagrams use a layered layout (each node drawn once, routed edges, TD/BT/LR/RL); unsupported diagram types show their source in a titled box
- Supports flowcharts/graphs, state, class and ER diagrams, sequence diagrams, pie charts, Gantt charts, mindmaps
- Unknown diagram types get fallback rendering

### Admonitions
- GitHub-style admonition blocks: [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING], [!CAUTION], with custom titles ([!NOTE] Title)
- Obsidian callouts ([!info], [!bug], [!example], ...; +/- fold markers ignored) mapped onto the same colours
- Each type has a distinct color and icon

### Wikilinks
- Converts [[target]] to [target](target.md)
- Converts [[target|display text]] to [display text](target.md)
- Preserves existing file extensions
- Skips wikilinks inside code blocks and inline code

### Interactive TUI
- Built on ratatui with crossterm backend
- Multi-tab: open multiple files, switch with Tab/Shift+Tab
- In-document search with highlighted matches; press Enter then n/N to cycle results, Esc to clear
- Keyboard link opening: press f to label on-screen links, then a letter to open web/mail links or follow a relative .md link
- Help overlay: press ? for a popup of the active keybindings
- Table of contents sidebar showing heading structure, tracks scroll position
- Interactive TOC: o focuses it (opening it if closed); j/k/arrows move, g/G first/last, Ctrl+d/Ctrl+u page, Enter jumps (recorded in back/forward history), h/l fold subheadings, / filters headings as you type, Esc returns; click a heading to jump, the wheel over the sidebar scrolls it
- Navigation history with back/forward ([ ] keys or Alt+Arrow)
- e opens the current local file in $VISUAL / $EDITOR (fallback vi; notepad on Windows) at the line of the heading being read (+N for vi/vim/nvim/nano/emacs/kak/micro, --goto file:N for VS Code/Codium/Cursor, file:N for subl/zed/hx), then reloads it and keeps the position; on Windows a bare editor name is looked up on PATH with PATHEXT, so .cmd/.bat shims such as code.cmd work; stdin and URL documents cannot be edited
- Mouse wheel scrolling, click a link to follow it (same path as f: browser for web/mail, in-app for .md and #anchor), plus drag-to-select (can be disabled via behavior.mouse_capture so the terminal handles clicks/selection instead)
- Event-driven redraw (no CPU when idle) and virtualized rendering for large documents
- Responsive to terminal resizing; shows a message instead of breaking on very small terminals

### File Browser
- Run `ink` with no args (TTY) or `ink .` or `ink <directory>`
- Interactive list of all .md files found recursively
- Filter with /, navigate with j/k/arrows, open with Enter
- Skips hidden files and common non-doc directories (node_modules, target, etc.)
- README files sorted first
- Browser opens a file then exits by default; press Shift+B to reopen, or set behavior.browser_loop = true to return automatically

### Themes
- 8 built-in themes: dark, light, dracula, catppuccin, nord, tokyo-night, gruvbox, solarized
- Auto-detection of terminal background (dark/light) by querying the terminal (OSC 11), falling back to COLORFGBG
- 24-bit, 256-colour and 16-colour output chosen from the terminal; --ascii (or [behavior] ascii = true) draws borders, bullets and markers in plain ASCII, automatic on the Linux console and non-UTF-8 locales
- --no-mouse leaves the mouse to the terminal for one session
- Live theme preview with T key; the chosen theme is saved to config
- ink --list-themes lists all available themes (built-in + custom)
- 30+ customizable color properties per theme
- Custom themes via TOML files in the themes/ folder of the ink config directory ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ink/themes/ when set)
- Honors NO_COLOR and quantizes 24-bit colors to the 256-color palette on non-truecolor terminals (truecolor detected via COLORTERM, WT_SESSION, or TERM_PROGRAM vscode/ghostty/WezTerm/iTerm.app)

### Other Features
- Presentation mode: split markdown on --- separators with --slides (navigate with arrows/space, slide counter in the status bar)
- Watch mode: auto-reload on file changes with --watch
- Plain output mode: output without TUI for piping with --plain; automatic when stdout is not a terminal
- --color auto|always|never (default auto): color and OSC 8 links only when stdout is a terminal; precedence is --color, then NO_COLOR, then CLICOLOR_FORCE/FORCE_COLOR, then TERM=dumb, then the TTY check. Use --color=always for fzf previews or less -R; git textconv (`ink --plain`) gets clean text
- `ink -` reads the document from stdin
- Pager mode: on an interactive terminal, --plain pages long output through $PAGER (default less -R), like bat; --no-pager disables it
- --line-range START:END (also START:, :END, N; repeatable): render only those 1-based source lines; a cut code fence is reopened/closed; implies --plain
- Document outline: `ink outline <file>` shows heading structure
- Document stats: `ink stats <file>` shows word count, reading time, element counts
- Markdown diff: `ink diff <file_a> <file_b>` compares two files with a real Myers line diff
- Shell integration: `ink shell-setup bash|zsh|fish` prints config snippets
- Shell completions: `ink completions bash|zsh|fish|powershell|elvish`
- Man page: `ink man` (troff)
- URL fetching: open markdown from HTTP/HTTPS URLs directly (timeout- and size-capped)
- Stdin support: pipe markdown content to ink

### Security
- Strips terminal control/escape bytes (ESC, C0, C1, DEL) from all rendered text, covering both the TUI and --plain, preventing ANSI/OSC escape-sequence and hyperlink injection from untrusted markdown
- Link destinations are scheme-validated (http/https/mailto/relative only); javascript:, file:, data: and control-byte URLs are dropped
- Remote images off by default; SSRF protections when enabled (see Images)
- Relative file/image paths are canonicalized and contained to the document's directory; absolute paths rejected
- install.sh / install.ps1 verify a published SHA256SUMS manifest before installing; release assets carry signed build provenance (`gh attestation verify <file> --repo borghei/ink`); CI runs cargo audit

### Keybindings
- j/k/↑/↓: scroll up/down
- Space/PageDown: page down
- PageUp: page up
- G/End: jump to end
- Home: jump to start
- Ctrl+f/Ctrl+b: page down/up
- Ctrl+d/Ctrl+u: half-page down/up
- n/N: next/previous heading (cycles search matches after a search)
- /: search
- f: link-hint mode (open/follow links by letter; the overlay lists each link's text next to its URL; Y inside the overlay copies the URL instead); #heading and file.md#heading links jump to the heading, and [ goes back
- v/V: select text character-wise / line-wise (motions hjkl, arrows, w/b, 0/$, g/G, Ctrl+d/Ctrl+u; y copies, Esc cancels)
- Mouse: drag selects and copies on release; double-click selects a word, triple-click a line
- c: label the code blocks on screen and copy one's raw source by letter
- Y: copy the current section as markdown source
- ?: help overlay
- t: toggle table of contents
- T: theme picker (saved to config)
- Enter: follow first visible link
- [/]: navigation back/forward
- Tab/Shift+Tab: next/previous tab
- Shift+B: reopen file browser
- q/Esc/Ctrl+C: quit (first press clears an active search)
- Presets: default (vim-flavored), vim, emacs; fully customizable, two-key chords supported

## Configuration

Config file: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ink/config.toml when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is set; otherwise ~/.config/ink/config.toml (Linux), ~/Library/Application Support/ink/config.toml (macOS), %APPDATA%\ink\config.toml (Windows). `ink config path` prints the resolved location.

```toml
theme = "catppuccin"
width = 90
spacing = "normal"
toc = false
frontmatter = false

[behavior]
browser_loop = false   # return to browser after closing a doc
mouse_capture = true    # set false to let the terminal handle clicks/selection
clipboard = "auto"      # auto | osc52 | native | off — how copied text reaches the clipboard

[keybindings]
preset = "emacs"        # default | vim | emacs
```

## Technical Stack
- Language: Rust
- Markdown parser: comrak (GFM-compliant)
- TUI framework: ratatui + crossterm
- Syntax highlighting: syntect
- Image decoding: image crate
- CLI: clap
- License: Free to use, cannot be sold (see LICENSE)

## Links
- Repository: https://github.com/borghei/ink
- Website: https://borghei.github.io/ink/
- Author: Amin Borghei <borghei.mohammadamin@gmail.com>
- Crates.io: https://crates.io/crates/ink-md (install with `cargo install ink-md`, Rust 1.90+)
- Install script (macOS/Linux): `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/borghei/ink/main/install.sh | sh` (picks the glibc or static musl build; pin with INK_VERSION=v0.8.0, target dir INK_INSTALL_DIR)
- Install script (Windows): `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/borghei/ink/main/install.ps1 | iex` (x64/ARM64, installs to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ink)
- Prebuilt binaries: Linux amd64/arm64 (glibc 2.35+), static musl Linux amd64/arm64/armv7 (Alpine, older glibc, Raspberry Pi), macOS amd64/arm64, Windows amd64/arm64; .deb/.rpm and tar.gz/zip archives with man page and completions
